text:
mina: Heads-up — autotuner change in canary caused ~12% tail-latency regression on short sequences. Observed at 2:14am UTC in cluster-c.

jordan: ugh. which change? the cost-model weight or kernel scoring? :grimacing:

mina: kernel scoring. we now add arch_score + memory_bandwidth_pref to pick. fine for long seqs but for <=32 tokens it picked the tiled-gemm-v2 path instead of fast-eltwise.

liam: can you paste the pick telemetry for a sample request?

mina: sure — here's the telemetry blob we log (sanitized):

```
pick_reason: ["arch_score:0.72","seq_bucket:<=32","expected_throughput:8500","kernel_chosen:tiled-gemm-v2","score_breakdown":{"kernel_pref":0.42,"mem_pref":0.18,"latency_est":0.12}}```

ops-bot: deploy/canary-2026-03-05 finished — 3/4 hosts healthy, 1 host in degraded state. see: https://infra/internal/deploys/2026-03-05/canary-12 :rotating_light:

sophia: do we have perf counters to show why tiled-gemm is slower on short seqs? maybe kernel has poor micro-batching for <64 tokens.

mina: profiler snapshots show extra kernel launch overhead and lower occupancy for tiled-gemm on sm80 when seq<48. paste of perf log:

```
--- perf summary ---
request: short-seq (len=24)
kernel: tiled-gemm-v2
gpu-time-ms: 0.42
cpu-overhead-ms: 0.18
launches: 3
kv-cache-hits: 0
notes: low occupancy, small matmul sizes => kernel underutilized
---
```

jordan: interesting. autotuner probably favored memory_bandwidth_pref because of a couple of long-seq traces in the weight. we should make seq_bucket influence stronger than arch_score for tiny seqs.

liam: propose quick mitigation: set REDWOOD_KPICK_DEBUG=shortseq_favor_eltwise=true in canary env OR lower mem_pref weight by 0.25 for seq<=32. which is less risky?

mina: lowering mem_pref is safer globally. but for the fastest fix, we can flip an env flag to disable arch_score for seq<=32. command to toggle in staging:

```
# toggle pick heuristic
kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/runtime-canary REDWOOD_KPICK_DEBUG=disable_arch_score_for_shortseq=true
```

sophia: add a metric to telemetry: chosen_kernel_latency_est and observed_token_latency so we can compute mispredictions over time. right now we only log reason but not predicted vs observed.

mina: agreed. I'll add those fields. sample enriched log we want:

```
pick_reason: ... , predicted_token_latency_ms: 0.012, observed_token_latency_ms: 0.018
```

ops-bot: rollback action available: canary-12 -> canary-11 (last stable). open PR? :gear:

jordan: do the env flip in canary, add telemetry change as follow-up PR, and schedule a short A/B to measure. mina and liam can own.

liam: doing the env flip now. logging it here.

```
kubectl exec -it runtime-canary-0 -n runtime -- env | grep REDWOOD_KPICK_DEBUG
# none
kubectl -n runtime set env deploy/runtime-canary REDWOOD_KPICK_DEBUG=disable_arch_score_for_shortseq=true
# updated
```

mina: can you also enable verbose kernel pick trace for one host so we get full stack traces? set REDWOOD_KPICK_TRACE=host:runtime-canary-2. it will spam logs but worth it for root cause.

liam: done. traces enabled on runtime-canary-2. :done: we'll capture 5k short requests.

mina: initial quick numbers post-flip: median tail-latency for len<=32 improved 9%, event rate steady. still want the telemetry patch.

sophia: for the telemetry PR, include fields: seq_bucket, arch_id, kernel_candidates, score_components (list), predicted_latency, observed_latency, kv_cache_hits, host_arch, and debug_flags. keep everything short.

jordan: also add a safety rule in autotuner: if predicted_latency variance > 20% across runs for same seq_bucket, prefer historically stable kernel. we saw picks oscillate in last week.

mina: filing issues: https://redwood/issue/RT-4923 (short-seq gemm regression), https://redwood/issue/RT-4924 (telemetry enrichment). I'll attach logs and perf dumps.

liam: thanks. after PR lands, let's run the canary for 24h and then roll to remaining hosts.

ops-bot: alert: canary-12 host runtime-canary-2 log volume high due to kpick-trace — disk usage at 75%. monitor.

mina: noted. I'll rotate logs and throttle trace to sample 1%.

sophia: one more thought — we should add a microbenchmark that runs per-arch short-seq matmul to keep a small latency table for seq buckets. autotuner can consult that table instead of relying purely on dynamic scoring. less noisy.

jordan: yes. create a job under eng-runtime/benchmarks that emits the table. low-risk and powerful.

mina: OK — plan: 1) env flip (done), 2) telemetry PR (mina), 3) microbenchmark job (jordan), 4) autotuner weight tweak + safety rule (liam/jordan). I'll update RT-4923 with timeline.

liam: I'll keep an eye on canary metrics and post a summary in ~6h. :clock3: 

mina: thanks all. :thumbsup:
